passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Alligators and crocodiles are both large reptiles.
• Alligators have wide, U-shaped snouts.
• Crocodiles have narrower, V-shaped snouts.
• Alligators live mostly in fresh water, while many crocodiles can tolerate salt water.
stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the snouts of alligators and crocodiles. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: While alligators have wide, U-shaped snouts, crocodiles have narrower, V-shaped snouts.
Alligators and crocodiles are both large reptiles, and both have long, powerful snouts.
Alligators live mostly in fresh water, while many crocodiles can tolerate salt water.
Crocodiles have narrow, V-shaped snouts that help them catch fish in fresh and salt water.
steps: The goal is a difference in snouts.
The answer must describe both animals' snouts and contrast them.
Only one choice contrasts wide, U-shaped snouts with narrower, V-shaped ones.
One choice shows a similarity, one shows a difference in habitat, and one describes only crocodiles.
key: A "difference" goal needs both things compared, on the exact feature named.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
